extracted.intended_audience: IP professionals, patent/trademark applicants, and policymakers in Russia
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for state registration, renewal, transfer, and electronic filing of intellectual property rights (inventions, utility models, industrial designs, trademarks, appellations of origin, computer programs, databases, TICs) at Rospatent. Contains procedural requirements, allowed document forms, electronic-filing channels, timing/fee considerations, and publication rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of documents for state registration of a contracted disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: The composition of documents submitted for state registration of a contracted disposition of exclusive right may include one application signed by two parties or an application signed by one party with the attached agreement (paragraph 3 of Article 1232 of the Code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted filing forms: either a jointly signed single application or a single application signed by one party accompanied by the agreement. The report notes increasing receipt of applications signed by two parties; in 2018, 2,908 applications (9.8% of considered applications) were received without attaching any other supporting document (i.e., relying on the jointly signed application).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing availability and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Rospatent official website allows filing of applications for state registration of inventions, utility models, industrial designs, trademarks, appellations of origin, computer programs and databases; topographies of integrated circuits (TICs) are excluded from direct filing on the site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As of end-2019, electronic filing is increasingly used. The share of requests filed via the official website is usually higher than 90% for the state services provided there. Rospatent plans to expand electronic services. Note: for TICs applicants must use alternative channels (e.g., EPGU) as direct filing on Rospatent site is not available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Single Portal of Public Services (EPGU) and other electronic channels
rubrics_metrics.description: The Single Portal of Public Services (EPGU) is used to file certain state services and applications not provided directly at Rospatent website; it also supports fee payments and quality assessment of provision of state services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In 2019, electronic applications filed through EPGU increased substantially (e.g., 1,099 applications for CPs/DBs/TICs via EPGU; overall growth noted). EPGU is used for services that are among the most popular but not available on the Rospatent site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing via FIPS information systems for CPs and DBs
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic filing of applications for computer programs and databases via Rospatent website using FIPS information systems is available and expanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage increased from 1,912 requests in 2018 to 3,561 in 2019 (increase of 86.2%). Applicants are encouraged to use those channels where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observance of time limits for administrative procedures (processing-time standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: When considering applications for state registration of CPs, DBs, and TICs, Rospatent gives great attention to observance of time limits for execution of administrative procedures and reports average consideration times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported average times were significantly reduced from 2018 to 2019: for CPs and DBs, from 1.28 months (2018) to 0.44 months (2019); for TICs, from 1.23 months to 0.41 months. December 2019 averages: CPs 0.41 months, DBs 0.43 months, TICs 0.36 months. These numeric targets/benchmarks indicate expected processing-performance levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee incentive for including multiple objects in one application
rubrics_metrics.description: If several objects are included in the same application, the fee for the applicant should be significantly lower than filing separate applications for each object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report notes a 37% increase in the number of objects included in filed applications for certain groups (2019 vs 2018), attributing part of this behavior to the fee structure that makes a single multi-object application cheaper for applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible omission of supporting documents when application is jointly signed
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for state registration of a contracted disposition signed by two parties may be submitted without attaching other supporting documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practice increased: in 2018 a substantial number of applications (2,908) were received without additional supporting documents because they were jointly signed. Rospatent continues to accept such forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal schedule for industrial designs (maintenance fee periodicity)
rubrics_metrics.description: For industrial designs with a fixed date of issue later than January 1, 2015, the design patent maintenance fee is paid once every five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative changes to the maintenance-fee system for design patents (5-year payments) reduced the number of early terminations and restorations of design patents, since fees are less frequent though still due at the five-year intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of patents requires payment of restoration fees (economic barrier)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restoration of legal protection for patents requires payment of restoration fees, which can be substantial and act as a barrier, especially for individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided: the fee for restoration of a patent to an invention in the 18th year of its activity is 46,700 rubles, which is expensive for most individuals and affects restoration dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open license application publication requirement/practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for the possibility of granting a right to use an invention, utility model or industrial design (open license) are received and published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In 2019, 111 open-license applications were received and 104 were published. Over the last five years the number of such applications and publications has been stable, indicating the expectation that published open-license applications become publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Cabinet e-service functionality for applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Personal Cabinet' e-service (updated Jan 14, 2019) allows filing applications and managing drafts for certain IP objects and provides additional features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New functions include filing applications for industrial designs, computer programs and databases directly via the service; filing industrial design applications under the Hague Agreement; working on drafts and viewing filed applications (for those filed via the service). This is an operational requirement/guidance for electronic applicants.
